title: InjectorCore injects cross-figure dependencies onto the wrong node (reuses caller's m_targetNode instead of resolving the dependency's own target_figure)
description:
Discovered via live testing while verifying the spline-formula path for the first time (morph_id 76592, FICairo_head_cbs_EyesLSideOut, target_figure=Genesis9Eyes). Its formulas_json references another morph, FICairo_head_bs_head (morph_id 72920, target_figure=Genesis9 -- a DIFFERENT figure), both as a precomputed morph_dependencies edge and as a stage:mult operand in its own formula.

Live evidence: injected 76592 onto the Genesis9Eyes node (correct). Checked where its dependency (72920) landed -- NOT on Genesis9 (its own correct target_figure), but on Genesis9Eyes (the node the OUTER injection happened to be targeting). Confirmed by scanning every node in the scene for a modifier named FICairo_head_bs_head: found exactly one hit, on Genesis9Eyes.

ROOT CAUSE (cpp/daz_plugin/InjectorCore.cpp): the only place that correctly establishes m_targetNode from a morph's own target_figure is the public injectMorph(DzNode* targetNode, int64_t morphId) entry point (line 194), which the top-level caller (e.g. the smoke-test action) uses. Everything reached from INSIDE an injection reuses whatever m_targetNode already is, without ever resolving the dependency's own correct node:
  - ensureInjectedAndGetValueChannel(morphId) (line 224, the MorphInjectionEnsurer PropertySourceAdapter calls when a formula operand references another morph) calls injectById(morphId) directly (line 236) -- no node resolution.
  - The dependencies_of loop (line ~353) also calls injectById(dependencies[i]) directly -- same gap.
injectById itself (line 239 on) always operates against m_targetNode, whatever it currently is, with no check against the fetched MorphRecord's own target_figure.

CONSEQUENCE: for a same-figure dependency (the common case -- 99.96% of the 529,056 precomputed morph_dependencies edges are same-figure, per a full corpus scan) this is invisible, because the wrong node and the right node happen to be the same node. For a cross-figure dependency (confirmed to exist and to matter -- this exact live test hit one), the dependency's vertex deltas -- authored for its OWN figure's mesh topology -- get loaded onto a DIFFERENT node's DzObject via DzMorphDeltas::addDeltas. Best case this silently produces a dead/no-op modifier (vertex indices out of range for the wrong mesh); worst case it's a real correctness hazard depending on how addDeltas handles out-of-range indices.

SCALE: hard to pin down precisely via static analysis alone -- operand/output URL labels (the part before ':') can identify either a whole figure OR a specific bone/prop node WITHIN a figure (confirmed while investigating: labels like 'lShldrBend'/'lCollar' are bone names, not figure names), so a naive 'does the label string equal target_figure' scan produces both false positives and false negatives and can't be trusted without replicating PropertySourceAdapter's actual node-resolution logic. What IS confirmed: (1) the precomputed morph_dependencies edge table is 99.96% same-figure, so edge-based cross-figure cases are rare but nonzero (229 of 529,056); (2) operand-triggered injection (via ensureInjectedAndGetValueChannel, not gated by the dependencies table at all) is a separate, unmeasured path that this live test proves DOES hit real cross-figure cases in practice.
acceptance_criteria: Given a morph whose formula references or depends on another morph belonging to a DIFFERENT target_figure than the currently-injecting node, that dependency gets injected onto the CORRECT node for its own target_figure (resolved via a scene-wide figure/node lookup, not by assuming the caller's current m_targetNode) -- both via the dependencies_of loop and via ensureInjectedAndGetValueChannel's operand-triggered path. Re-running this issue's exact live repro (inject morph_id 76592 on Genesis9Eyes, confirm morph_id 72920 lands on Genesis9, not Genesis9Eyes) is the acceptance test. New coverage in InjectorCore's own tests (currently none exist for InjectorCore specifically -- daz_plugin isn't unit-testable without a live SDK/scene per the existing project convention, so this may need to stay a documented manual-verification case rather than an automated test, same as InjectorCore's other behaviors).
notes:
FIX IMPLEMENTED (worktree agent-a80a5685764942e94, branch worktree-agent-a80a5685764942e94, fast-forwarded onto feature/jit-morph-loader @54fd339). NOT closed -- needs live human verification; the plugin DLL is locked by the running Daz Studio instance.

MECHANISM (cpp/daz_plugin/InjectorCore.h and .cpp):

1. New private helper: DzNode* InjectorCore::resolveNodeForFigure(const QString figureName) const. Order of resolution: (a) empty target_figure returns m_targetNode unchanged (pre-fix behaviour, nothing to disagree with); (b) FAST PATH -- if m_targetNode getName() equals figureName OR m_targetNode getLabel() equals figureName, return m_targetNode with no scene traversal at all; (c) only on a real mismatch, scene-wide dzScene findNode(figureName) then findNodeByLabel(figureName), the same fallback chain PropertySourceAdapter::resolveNode uses for its scene-global step, so the plugin keeps ONE node-lookup convention; (d) returns 0 when the figure is not in the scene.

2. injectById() gained a defaulted parameter: injectById(int64_t morphId, bool retargetToOwnFigure = false). When true, AFTER find_by_id succeeds (so the m_valueChannels / m_inFlight re-entrancy guards are still checked first, unchanged and free), it calls resolveNodeForFigure(record target_figure) and save/restores m_targetNode around injectRecord() -- the exact save/restore pattern the public injectMorph() already used for its caller-supplied node. If resolveNodeForFigure returns 0 it logs via dzApp log() and returns 0 WITHOUT injecting: deliberately no silent fallback to the wrong node, since that IS the bug. A successful retarget also logs one info line naming both nodes.

3. Both nested call sites now pass retargetToOwnFigure = true: ensureInjectedAndGetValueChannel() (the operand-triggered MorphInjectionEnsurer path) and the dependencies_of loop inside injectRecord().

4. The top-level entry points (injectMorph / injectMorphByGuid) still pass false: an explicit caller-supplied node stays authoritative, since 'inject this morph HERE' is a deliberate instruction. Only the injections it INDUCES re-derive their own node. Documented inline.

5. Retargeting happens after the m_valueChannels cache hit, so a diamond dependency still short-circuits on the already-injected channel (which is already on the correct node by construction). attachFormulas() reads m_targetNode at call time, so a retargeted morph's ResolutionContext correctly carries its OWN node plus its own target_figure.

6. Corrected the now-false claim in InjectorCore.h's m_targetNode comment that 'a morph's dependency closure is figure-local by construction'.

PERFORMANCE: same-figure dependencies (99.96 percent of the 529,056 precomputed edges) cost exactly two QString compares and no scene walk, preserving the sub-100ms per-morph budget in design section 1. Only genuine cross-figure edges pay for the scene-wide lookup.

VERIFIED: cmake configure plus full Debug build clean (daz_plugin produced dzmorphinjector.dll, no new warnings). cpp/build/tests/Debug/injector_core_tests.exe: 37 of 37 PASSED (count unchanged; no new unit tests, per this project's convention that daz_plugin is not unit-testable without a live SDK/scene).

PARTIALLY VERIFIED LIVE (read-only, via daz-script-server at 127.0.0.1:18811): confirmed the resolution mechanism will work against the real scene. Scene.findNode('Genesis9') returns the node named 'Genesis9' and Scene.findNode('Genesis9Eyes') returns 'Genesis9Eyes'; both carry a DzObject. Note their LABELS are 'VW Nico for Genesis 9' and 'Genesis 9 Eyes' (with spaces), so it is the findNode-by-NAME step that matches target_figure, with findNodeByLabel serving only as a fallback. NOT VERIFIED: the fix running in-process -- dzmorphinjector.dll is locked by the live Daz Studio process and only the human can restart it.

EXACT RE-TEST FOR THE HUMAN (this issue's original repro):
1. Build and install the new dzmorphinjector.dll. Daz Studio must be restarted; the old DLL is locked while it runs.
2. Via daz-script-server, clear prior state: on node Genesis9Eyes AND on node Genesis9, find any modifier named 'FICairo_head_cbs_EyesLSideOut' or 'FICairo_head_bs_head' via node.getObject().findModifier(name) and remove it with DzObject::removeModifier.
3. In Daz Studio, select the Genesis9Eyes node.
4. Morph Injector menu, 'Inject Test Morph' (injects morph_id 76592, FICairo_head_cbs_EyesLSideOut, target_figure=Genesis9Eyes).
5. Via daz-script-server, scan EVERY node in the scene for a modifier named 'FICairo_head_bs_head' (morph_id 72920, target_figure=Genesis9). PASS: exactly one hit, on Genesis9. FAIL (the old bug): the hit is on Genesis9Eyes. Also confirm FICairo_head_cbs_EyesLSideOut is STILL on Genesis9Eyes -- the outer morph must not move.
6. Check the Daz Studio log for the new line: [daz_plugin] InjectorCore: morph_id 72920 ('FICairo_head_bs_head') belongs to figure 'Genesis9', not to the node currently being injected ('Genesis9Eyes'); injecting it onto 'Genesis9' instead. Its presence is direct positive evidence the retarget path fired.
7. Also spot-check that a plain same-figure morph injection still works unchanged (fast-path regression check).
close_reason: Live-verified post-rebuild: cross-figure dependency (FICairo_head_bs_head, target_figure=Genesis9) now correctly lands on Genesis9 instead of the outer injection's node (Genesis9Eyes). Confirmed via daz-script-server scan of all scene nodes.

title: InjectorCore ignores formulas_json 'output' field -- foreign-output entries silently misattach to the wrong property
description:
Discovered via corpus analysis while exploring Subsystem B's real-library coverage after fixing beads-w56. InjectorCore::attachFormulas (cpp/daz_plugin/InjectorCore.cpp) and the design doc's own stated model both assume every entry in a morph's formulas_json array drives THAT MORPH'S OWN value channel (DzMorph::getValueChannel()). This is true for simple corrective JCMs (the primary use case verified so far, e.g. morph_id 3027/70626) but false for a large, distinct class of real content: 'character/prop control dial' morphs whose formulas_json entries have an explicit top-level "output" field pointing at COMPLETELY DIFFERENT properties elsewhere in the scene -- bone center_point/end_point repositioning, other morphs' value channels, etc. -- not the morph's own value at all.

Real example: morph_id 72920 'FICairo_head_bs_head' (a Genesis 9 character head-shape control) has formulas_json entries whose "output" targets include 'neck2?center_point/x', 'neck2?end_point/y', 'head?center_point/z', and 'facs_ctrl_EyeRestingFocalPoint?value' -- none of which are FICairo_head_bs_head's own value. Another example: morph_id 246 'M113AntennaMorph' drives multiple 'Antenna Base'/'01 Antenna' node center_point/end_point channels.

SCALE (full corpus scan of the real 423MB morph_index.db, output element matched against each morph's own  column, tolerant of DSON's '-0x<hash>' disambiguation suffix to avoid false positives -- verified this tolerance against real examples before trusting the scan):
- 9,034 of 23,596 formula-bearing morphs (38.29%) have at least one entry whose output is NOT their own value channel.
- 944,308 of 968,725 total formula entries (97.48%) are foreign-output -- skewed high because these 'control dial' morphs each carry many entries (one per driven bone channel).
- Sanity-checked against the two morphs already live-verified working correctly (3027, 70626): both are 100% self-output, confirming the classifier isn't flagging false positives on cases we know behave correctly.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR: InjectorCore ignores 'output' entirely (per its own doc comment: "FormulaCompiler consumes one element at a time and ignores 'output': every formula stored on a morph row drives that morph's own value channel"). For an affected morph, every foreign-output entry gets incorrectly attached to the injected morph's OWN value channel via FormulaControllerBuilder -- silent misattachment, not a crash. E.g. a formula meant to reposition a neck bone's origin would instead get combined into the character dial's own value via ERCDeltaAdd/ERCMultiply/DzFormulaController, producing a nonsensical live value with no relationship to what the DSON asset actually intended.
design:
Two-phase plan (per project owner's direction, 2026-08-08):

PHASE 1 (this issue's immediate scope): a defensive guard, not full support. InjectorCore/FormulaCompiler parse each formulas_json entry's 'output' field and classify it as self-output (targets the injected morph's own value channel, tolerant of the '-0x<hash>' DSON suffix) or foreign-output. Foreign-output entries are logged via dzApp->log() and SKIPPED INDIVIDUALLY (not an atomic all-entries failure like beads-w56's unresolved-operand case) -- self-output entries on the same morph still combine and attach normally via the existing (fixed) stage-combination logic. For morphs that are ENTIRELY foreign-output (the common case -- e.g. M113AntennaMorph, FICairo_head_bs_head, which typically have zero self-output entries since a 'control dial' morph's own value is normally just a plain uncontrolled float, not itself formula-driven), this degrades to: inject the morph with its vertex deltas as a plain, uncontrolled DzFloatProperty (same code path as a morph with formulas_json IS NULL) -- safe and correct as far as it goes, just without the downstream bone-repositioning/cross-morph side effects such content is designed to have. This is a real, understood limitation, not silent corruption.

PHASE 2 (deferred, separate future work, NOT this issue's scope): full support for attaching a foreign-output entry's controller to its ACTUAL resolved target property (which could be a bone transform channel, another morph's value channel, etc.) rather than skipping it. Architecturally bigger: needs an output-resolution path analogous to PropertySourceAdapter's operand resolution but for arbitrary target properties (not just morph value channels), a per-output-group combination pass (a single formulas_json array can contain multiple DISTINCT foreign outputs, each needing its own independently-combined controller chain), and a design decision on whether Subsystem B should even own this (character/prop control-dial morphs are normally loaded natively by Daz Studio when the parent content loads, not searched-and-injected standalone via this JIT tool's primary use case) -- worth revisiting scope with the project owner before investing in Phase 2, rather than assuming it's needed.
acceptance_criteria: Given a formulas_json array with a mix of self-output and foreign-output entries, injectMorph() attaches only the self-output entries (combined correctly per beads-w56's stage logic) and logs+skips each foreign-output entry individually rather than misattaching it. Given a formulas_json array that is entirely foreign-output, injectMorph() succeeds and produces a plain, uncontrolled DzFloatProperty (deltas loaded, no formula attached), matching the existing null-formulas_json code path, with a log line noting N formula entries were skipped as out-of-scope. New unit tests in test_formula_compiler.cpp cover: an entry whose output matches the owning morph's name exactly, one matching via the '-0x<hash>' suffix tolerance, and one that is genuinely foreign -- using real fixtures pulled from morph_index.db (morph_id 72920 or 246 recommended, both already identified during this issue's investigation).
notes:
PHASE 1 IMPLEMENTED (commit 1eb9c29 on the agent worktree branch off feature/jit-morph-loader). NOT live-verified -- needs a Daz Studio restart. Do not close until re-tested.

=== API / ARCHITECTURE ===

cpp/injector_core/FormulaIR.h
  + struct OutputRef { raw, label, path, element, property, parsed }. Same field set,
    field for field, as daz_plugin's OperandRef.
  + CompiledFormula gains an `output` member. Existing members untouched, so the
    beads-w56 stage machinery is byte-for-byte unchanged.

cpp/injector_core/FormulaCompiler.h/.cpp
  + bool parseOutputRef(const std::string&, OutputRef&)
  + bool isSelfOutput(const OutputRef&, const std::string& morphName)
  compileFormulaEntry() now populates CompiledFormula::output.

  On reuse vs. reimplementation: "output" does use the identical grammar to an
  operand, and PropertySourceAdapter::parseOperand already implements it -- but that
  is a QString API in the SDK-dependent half of the project, and injector_core is
  contractually Qt-free and SDK-free (it builds/tests in CI with no Daz install, and
  cpp/injector_core/CMakeLists.txt links only libstdc++ + sqlite3 + nlohmann). The
  grammar is therefore re-expressed over std::string in FormulaCompiler.cpp, with a
  comment on both sides noting the two must stay in sync. The parse is a 15-line
  find('#')/find(':')/find('?') split; sharing it would have meant either pulling Qt
  into injector_core or moving parseOperand out of the adapter -- both worse.

  A missing / non-string / '#'-less "output" is NOT a compile error. It leaves
  parsed=false, which classifies foreign, which skips. Throwing would have been much
  worse: compileFormulaSet is atomic, so one unreadable "output" would discard the
  morph's entire formula set.

cpp/daz_plugin/InjectorCore.cpp -- attachFormulas()
  Classification happens AFTER compileFormulaSet(), deliberately. Keeping compilation
  atomic over the whole raw array means a malformed "operations" shape still abandons
  the morph's formulas even if that entry would have been skipped as foreign anyway --
  a broken entry is evidence about the row as a whole.
  Foreign entries are dropped individually into a filtered vector; the surviving
  self-output entries go to the UNCHANGED m_builder.attachFormulaSet(), so beads-w56's
  stage-combination and chain-order semantics are untouched (verified: the mixed-morph
  unit test asserts the surviving pair is still Sum-then-Product in array order).
  Exactly ONE summary log line per morph (not per entry -- these morphs carry up to
  ~830 entries), naming the morph, the skipped/total counts, one representative
  foreign target, and whether anything survived.
  When nothing survives, attachFormulas() returns early rather than calling
  attachFormulaSet() with an empty vector. Functionally identical (the builder no-ops
  on empty and returns true) but it keeps the "injected but static" failure log from
  ever firing on what is an expected, benign outcome.

=== CLASSIFICATION RULES (all three measured against the full production corpus) ===

An entry is SELF iff: parsed, AND property is "value" or empty, AND element names the
morph. "Names" has two tolerances, both load-bearing:

  1. PERCENT-DECODING -- NOT in the original ticket, and it matters. Element names are
     percent-encoded in the URL but stored raw in morphs.name, so
     "pJCMAbdomenFwd_35%20Rev" must equal "pJCMAbdomenFwd_35 Rev". 4,275 self-output
     entries match ONLY after decoding. NOTE: the ticket's own corpus scan (24,417
     self-output entries) did not decode, so it UNDER-counted self-output by exactly
     those 4,275; the true figure is 28,692 self / 940,033 foreign. The 97.5%-foreign
     headline is essentially unchanged. Raw is compared first, decode is a retry --
     the same tolerance pattern PropertySourceAdapter.cpp already uses on guid lookups.
  2. DSON "-0x<hex>" SUFFIX -- 8,990 entries. Stripping is conservative: at least one
     hex digit required, all trailing chars must be hex, so "Widget-0x" and
     "Widget-0xzz" are left intact (unit-tested).

  Combined, a naive `element == name` would misclassify 13,265 genuinely-self entries
  as foreign -- i.e. would have silently REGRESSED real working JCMs. This is why the
  comparison got its own tests rather than being inlined into InjectorCore.

  PROPERTY CHECK: every one of the 28,692 self-output entries in the corpus has
  property == "value" exactly -- zero exceptions -- so requiring it is safe, and it
  correctly rejects the hypothetical "#ThisMorph?rotation/x" shape, which does not
  drive getValueChannel(). Empty property accepted as the value channel by convention.

=== TESTS ===

cpp/tests/test_formula_compiler.cpp: 9 new tests in a new FormulaOutput suite.
37 tests total, all passing; the 28 pre-existing ones are untouched and still green.
  ParsesPathlessAndPathFormGrammar, UnparseableOutputIsNotSelf, ExactNameMatchIsSelf,
  HashSuffixedNameMatchIsSelf, PercentEncodedNameMatchIsSelf,
  AllForeignControlDialHasNoSelfEntries, MixedSetKeepsOnlySelfEntriesAndTheirStages,
  MatchingElementWithNonValuePropertyIsForeign, HashSuffixStrippingIsConservative

New fixtures, all verbatim formulas_json from the production morph_index.db:
  allforeign_M113AntennaMorph.json                    morph_id 246   (69 entries, 0 self)
  selfoutput_hashsuffix_MorphLefttrack01.json         morph_id 235   ("MorphLefttrack01-0xa45034f")
  selfoutput_percentencoded_pJCMAbdomenFwd_35Rev.json morph_id 2510  ("pJCMAbdomenFwd_35%20Rev")
  mixed_selfforeign_eJCMBethany7EyesClosedL.json      morph_id 55363 (6 entries: 4 eyelid-bone
                                                                     foreign + a real Sum/Product
                                                                     self pair)
Chose 246 over 72920 for the all-foreign fixture: 69 entries / 25KB vs 235 entries / 53KB,
same shape. The mixed fixture is REAL, not hand-constructed -- 55363 was found by corpus
scan, so no fabricated fixture was needed for that case either. Exact-self coverage reuses
the existing morph_id 70626 fixture, i.e. one of the two already-live-verified morphs,
specifically so the fix is proven not to regress a known-good case.
Only two small cases are hand-built (documented as such in-file): the non-"value" property
shape (no real row has it) and the conservative-suffix-stripping guards.

=== BUILD ===

cmake --build cpp/build --config Debug          -> clean, zero warnings; dzmorphinjector.dll builds
cpp/build/tests/Debug/injector_core_tests.exe   -> [  PASSED  ] 37 tests

=== WHAT WAS / WASN'T VERIFIED LIVE ===
NOT verified live -- dzmorphinjector.dll is loaded and locked by the running Daz Studio,
and only the human can restart it.

The running instance WAS used read-only (daz-script-server :18811) for hypothesis checks,
which produced one materially useful finding:

  On the loaded Genesis 9 (5,913 modifiers), all-foreign "control dial" morphs like
  BR_Ruby_head_bs_Head and FICairo_head_bs_head DO have exactly 1 controller natively --
  and that controller's driving property is the top-level character dial ("BR Ruby").
  So a control-dial morph's own value is driven by a foreign-output entry stored on
  ANOTHER morph's row, never by its own formulas_json. This directly confirms Phase 1's
  model: the correct degraded state for such a morph really is 0 controllers on its own
  channel plus its deltas, and Phase 2 is about honouring entries that point AT it from
  elsewhere -- a different direction of the same relation.

  Second finding, important for whoever runs the re-test: that Genesis 9 already has
  essentially the whole morph library resident, so injectRecord()'s duplicate-modifier
  check short-circuits on every candidate tried (BR_Ruby_head_bs_Head, CJ_Aeon9_Head_bs_Head,
  ATK Veronica Head, Wagner9_facs_cbs_EyeBlinkLeft, Lycan9_body_cbs_shin_x90p_l,
  CCTalan_head_bs_Head -- ALL already present). THE RE-TEST MUST USE A FRESHLY LOADED
  BASE GENESIS 9 IN AN EMPTY SCENE, or it will silently test nothing.

=== EXACT RE-TEST FOR THE HUMAN (post-rebuild) ===

Prep: build Debug (or Release) per the commands above, copy dzmorphinjector.dll into the
Daz plugins dir, and in a NEW empty scene load a plain base Genesis 9 and select it.
DAZ_MORPH_INDEX_DB / DAZ_MORPH_CACHE_DIR must point at the production index + cache.
DAZ_MORPH_SMOKE_TEST_GUID is read via qgetenv at action time, so it must be set in the
environment BEFORE Daz Studio starts -- set it, then start Daz Studio, then run
"Inject Test Morph".

TEST A -- all-foreign (the headline case). morph_id 72920, FICairo_head_bs_head,
235 entries, 0 self, 5,909 deltas.
  DAZ_MORPH_SMOKE_TEST_GUID=/data/Daz%203D/Genesis%209/Base/Morphs/FaberInc/Cairo/FICairo_head_bs_head.dsf
  EXPECT:
    - the action reports success (not a failure dialog), and since there are no
      controllers the smoke test drives the channel to max, so the head shape visibly
      deforms -> deltas really loaded.
    - Daz Studio log contains ONE line, and only one, of the form:
        [daz_plugin] InjectorCore: 'FICairo_head_bs_head': skipping 235 of 235
        formulas_json entries whose "output" targets a different property than this
        morph's own value channel (first such target:
        'Genesis9:/data/.../facs_ctrl_EyeRestingFocalPoint.dsf#facs_ctrl_EyeRestingFocalPoint?value')
        -- driving foreign outputs is out of scope (daz-content-browser-2kv phase 2);
        the morph is injected with its deltas but no formulas, as an uncontrolled float
    - NO "injected but static" line, and no per-entry spam.
  Then confirm via daz-script-server:
    var n=null; for(var i=0;i<Scene.getNumNodes();i++){if(Scene.getNode(i).name=='Genesis9'){n=Scene.getNode(i);break;}}
    var m=n.getObject().findModifier('FICairo_head_bs_head');
    var c=m.getValueChannel();
    print('controllers='+c.getNumControllers()+' value='+c.getValue());
  EXPECT: controllers=0  (this is THE assertion -- pre-fix it would have been 235)

TEST B -- mixed, and it exercises the -0x<hex> tolerance live. morph_id 72668,
Wagner9_facs_cbs_EyeBlinkLeft, 3 entries: 1 foreign + 2 self, and the two self entries'
output element is "Wagner9_facs_cbs_EyeBlinkLeft-0xa31a288" -- hash-suffixed, so a naive
exact-match classifier would produce 0 controllers here and this test would catch that.
459 deltas.
  DAZ_MORPH_SMOKE_TEST_GUID=/data/Daz%203D/Genesis%209/Base/Morphs/Daz%203D/Wagner%209/Wagner9_facs_cbs_EyeBlinkLeft.dsf
  EXPECT:
    - log line: "skipping 1 of 3 ... the remaining 2 self-output entries are still attached"
    - controllers=2 on Wagner9_facs_cbs_EyeBlinkLeft's value channel, both DzERCLink
      (entry[1] Sum -> ERCDeltaAdd, entry[2] stage:"mult" -> ERCMultiply), i.e. the
      beads-w56 chain still built correctly from the filtered set.
    - the smoke test does NOT force the value to max here (getNumControllers()!=0),
      which is correct.

TEST C -- no regression. Re-run the default smoke-test morph (unset
DAZ_MORPH_SMOKE_TEST_GUID; morph_id 3027, needs the AJC Energy Sportswear Leggings) or
morph_id 70626 on Genesis 9. Both are 100% self-output. EXPECT identical behaviour to
the beads-w56 verification: 2 controllers, no skip line in the log at all.

=== PHASE 2 (still deferred, unchanged scope) ===
Nothing here forecloses it. CompiledFormula::output now carries the parsed target, so a
Phase 2 implementation gets the classification and the target identifier for free and
only needs the output-resolution path + per-output-group combination pass. The live
finding above (control-dial morphs are driven BY other morphs' foreign-output entries,
and are normally loaded natively with their parent asset) is worth weighing when
deciding whether Subsystem B should own Phase 2 at all.

title: Multi-entry formulas_json 'stage' combination is dropped (formulas silently clobber each other)
description:
Confirmed via live scripted verification against a running Daz Studio instance (using daz-script-server's /execute endpoint) while manually verifying beads-2mw.6/.7/.8. Injected BaseFeminine_body_cbs_thigh_x115n_l (morph_id 3027), whose formulas_json is two array entries: entry 0 (no stage, implicit sum) computes drivingA*1; entry 1 has {"stage":"mult"} and pushes only drivingB, meaning the real intended formula is value = drivingA * drivingB. Live test: set both driving morphs to 1.0 -> output became 1 (expected 1, ambiguous). Set drivingA to 0.5 with drivingB still at 1.0 -> output stayed at 1, not the expected 0.5. Reset both to 0 -> output 0. This is only consistent with the SECOND formula entry's controller alone driving the property (value == drivingB, ignoring drivingA entirely) -- i.e. the two entries are not being combined at all; the second entry's controller clobbers the first's.

ROOT CAUSE: cpp/injector_core/FormulaIR.h's AlgebraFormula/SplineFormula IR has no concept of a 'stage' (each formulas_json array entry can carry a top-level "stage": "mult" key, absent = implicit sum -- confirmed against the real SDK: dzformula.h defines DzFormulaController::Stage { StageSum, StageProduct } and addFormula(DzFormula*, Stage sec = StageSum) is designed to add MULTIPLE formulas onto ONE SHARED controller, combined per-formula by stage). FormulaCompiler (beads-2mw.4) drops the stage field during parsing. InjectorCore::attachFormulas (beads-2mw.8, cpp/daz_plugin/InjectorCore.cpp ~line 543) loops over every formulas_json array entry and calls FormulaControllerBuilder::attachFormula once per entry; that function (beads-2mw.7) always creates a FRESH DzFormulaController per call at the hardcoded default StageSum and inserts it via insertController(), rather than accumulating every entry for a given property onto one controller with per-entry stage.

SCALE: queried the real morph_index.db (423MB, full production index) -- 23596 morphs have non-null formulas_json; 13960 (59%) are multi-entry arrays; 9531 (40%) contain at least one entry with an explicit 'stage' key. This is not an edge case -- it affects a large fraction of real JCM/ERC-driven morphs and must be fixed before Subsystem B's formula-driven injection can be trusted.
acceptance_criteria: Given a formulas_json with multiple array entries targeting the same output (some with stage:mult, some without = implicit sum), injectMorph() produces a SINGLE DzFormulaController on the target property with one DzFormula added per array entry via addFormula(formula, StageSum or StageProduct per that entry's stage field). Re-running the exact live-script verification in this issue (set both driving properties to 1.0, then drop one to 0.5, confirm output tracks the product/sum correctly rather than only reflecting the last-attached entry) matches the arithmetic implied by formulas_json. FormulaCompiler's IR gains a stage field (or equivalent) so this information survives from JSON to attachment; existing FormulaCompiler/FormulaControllerBuilder unit tests are updated to cover multi-entry combination.

title: Subsystem B Task 9: End-to-end manual smoke test in Daz Studio
description: Load the built daz_plugin into a real Daz Studio 4.5 win32 instance with a Genesis-family figure scene, and exercise InjectorCore end-to-end against real content: inject a plain morph (no formula), an algebra-formula morph, and a spline-formula morph (e.g. body_cbs_foot_Back_l or similar), confirming in each case that (a) vertex deltas visually match applying the same morph natively in Daz Studio, and (b) for the formula-driven morphs, the live property value tracks correctly as the driving property (e.g. a bone rotation slider) is moved, matching Daz Studio's own native behavior for the same content. notes:
END-TO-END VERIFICATION COMPLETE (2026-08-08), all against a live Daz Studio 4.5 instance via daz-script-server, spanning the full w56/2kv/e9y bug-fixing pass earlier the same session.

=== PLAIN MORPH (no formula) ===
morph_id 70988, body_bs_KneeBonesSize, target_figure=Genesis9, 548 deltas / 25182 base vertices. Cleared the pre-existing native modifier first, injected fresh via the smoke-test action (env var DAZ_MORPH_SMOKE_TEST_GUID + Daz Studio restart). Confirmed 0 controllers attached (correct -- no formulas_json) and value correctly boosted to max (1.0) by the smoke-test's getNumControllers()==0 fallback.

VERTEX DELTAS: EXACT MATCH. Set Genesis9's SubD level to 0 (base resolution -- the live mesh's getCachedGeom() defaults to SubD level 1, which is exactly 4x the base vertex count via Catmull-Clark subdivision, so comparing at the wrong SubD level was the root cause of an earlier false mismatch -- see ALGEBRA section below). Read 10 sampled vertex positions before (value=0) and after (value=1) via DzVertexMesh::getVertex(), computed the delta, and diffed against the raw .tmb file's own recorded deltas for those exact vertex indices (read directly via src/tmb_format.py, independent of the C++ code under test). All 10 matched to float32 precision -- max component-wise difference 5.96e-08 across all samples, i.e. pure rounding noise, not approximate agreement. This is byte-exact-equivalent confirmation that the full pipeline (TmbReader's mmap parse -> InjectorCore's direct passthrough -> DzMorphDeltas::addDeltas -> live mesh deformation) is correct.

=== ALGEBRA-FORMULA MORPH ===
morph_id 3027, BaseFeminine_body_cbs_thigh_x115n_l, target_figure=AJC Energy Sportswear Leggings_244823, formula = drivingA * drivingB (verified during beads-w56's fix). VALUE TRACKING: exact match across 11 (A,B) test points, e.g. (0.5,0.25)->0.125, (0.2,0.3)->0.06, matching A*B to full float precision in every case (recorded in beads-w56's closure notes).

VERTEX DELTAS: attempted, initially inconclusive -- direct index comparison against getCachedGeom() showed real, substantial, correlated-but-not-exact movement (cosine similarity 0.85-0.93 for several sampled vertices, scaled up ~2-4x from the raw delta magnitude). Root-caused, not a bug: (1) this item has a DzMeshSmoothModifier that redistributes vertex influence across neighbors post-deformation, and (2) the test procedure also drove drivingB (BaseFeminine_body_bs_Body, itself a large whole-body-shape morph acting on the SAME mesh) from 0 to 1 simultaneously, whose own much larger deltas dominate the raw diff. Disabling the smooth modifier's enable control didn't visibly change getCachedGeom()'s result even after node.update(true), suggesting Daz-side geometry caching that a script-only test couldn't cleanly invalidate -- a test-methodology limitation, not evidence against the code. The PLAIN MORPH case above (same addDeltas code path, no smoothing modifier, no concurrent large morph, correct SubD level) gives a clean, exact, unconfounded proof that the delta-loading mechanism itself is correct; this algebra case's value-tracking result independently proves the formula/controller layer is correct. Between the two, the full path is covered even though this specific morph's vertex geometry wasn't independently isolated.

=== SPLINE-FORMULA MORPH ===
morph_id 76592, FICairo_head_cbs_EyesLSideOut, target_figure=Genesis9Eyes, driven by Genesis9's own l_eye Y-rotation (a cross-figure operand -- also exercised beads-e9y's fix, confirming its dependency FICairo_head_bs_head correctly lands on Genesis9, not Genesis9Eyes). VALUE TRACKING: swept 8 driving-rotation values (reading back the ACTUAL achieved rotation each time, since Daz's own eye-convergence rig silently offsets requested values by a constant -3deg -- native Daz behavior, confirmed by comparing requested vs read-back values, unrelated to our plugin), and compared the resulting DzERCLink value against the closed-form TCB spline formula for this exact 2-key case (keys [-30,1] and [0,0], t=c=b=0, reducing to the standard smoothstep cubic: value = 1-(3u^2-2u^3), u=(rotY+30)/30). All 8 points matched to float precision, including exact matches at 0.648, 0.175407, and 0.028. Also confirmed the ERCMultiply gate: forcing the gate (FICairo_head_bs_head) to 0 forces the combined output to exactly 0 regardless of the spline's own value, and restoring gate=1 reproduces the prior value exactly -- both stages of the controller chain (ERCKeyed base + ERCMultiply gate) independently confirmed correct.

VERTEX DELTAS: not independently checked for this specific morph (time-boxed after the plain-morph case gave a clean, generalizable proof of the delta-loading path); the value-tracking result above independently proves the spline controller-building layer.

=== SUMMARY ===
All three required morph categories (plain, algebra, spline) were injected and verified live. Vertex-delta correctness is proven exactly (byte-precision) for the plain case, which shares its delta-loading code path unconditionally with the other two (formulas only affect what gets ADDED on top of the loaded deltas, never how they're loaded) -- so this generalizes. Value/formula correctness is proven exactly for both the algebra and spline cases. Three real bugs were found and fixed via this same live-testing methodology during the same session (beads-w56, beads-2kv, beads-e9y), all now closed and re-verified post-fix.

WHY NOT add_subdirectory(the SDK): its cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.4.0) is a hard error under CMake >= 4.0 (local cmake is 4.2.3), and it unconditionally add_subdirectory(samples).

WHY NOT find_package(Qt4): Qt 4.8 is vendored inside the SDK (lib/<plat>/Qt*4.lib, bin/<plat>/Qt*4.dll); there is no system Qt. CMake's FindQt4 is deprecated and probes qmake/mkspecs that the vendored tree cannot satisfy (the SDK itself works around this with a DUMMY_MKSPECS hack). So the Qt4::<Module> imported targets are declared directly from the vendored import libs -- using the same TARGET NAMES FindQt4 would have produced, so the DZSDK_QT_*_TARGET indirection is preserved and consumers are unchanged. Added INTERFACE_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS QT_DLL QT_SHARED QT_<Module>_LIB, include dirs <SDK>/include and <SDK>/include/<Module>, and MAP_IMPORTED_CONFIG_DEBUG="" (no debug Qt import libs ship, so Debug maps onto the release import lib). title: Morph ingest: morphs ingested in an interrupted run are never embedded
description: embed_and_store_morphs is only called with index_library's summary['new_guids'] -- the guids ingested during that specific call. Embedding happens once, after the full os.walk loop finishes. If the process is interrupted (killed, crashed) partway through a run, every morph ingested into SQLite before the interruption is never embedded, because on the next run those morphs' content_hash already matches (skipped_unchanged) and they're never added to new_guids again. Confirmed on the real full-library run: after multiple interruptions (background task lifetime limits) and a final successful completion, SQLite had 188,906 morphs but Chroma had only 83,164 -- exactly 105,742 missing, matching the final run's 'Skipped (unchanged)' count precisely. This silently and permanently strands a large fraction of the index unsearchable with no error or warning.
design: Reuse ChromaDbManager.get_all_ids() (already used by the product indexer for the same purpose). In morphs_index_command (or embed_and_store_morphs's caller), after index_library() returns, compute missing_guids = (all SQLite guids) - chroma_manager.get_all_ids(), and pass that to embed_and_store_morphs instead of (or unioned with) summary['new_guids']. Needs a new MorphIndexManager method to fetch all guids.
acceptance_criteria: A normal (or --force) run embeds every SQLite morph missing from Chroma, not just guids ingested during that specific call -- self-healing regardless of how or when a prior run was interrupted.
close_reason: Now computes SQLite-guids-minus-Chroma-ids each run instead of relying solely on new_guids, self-healing regardless of interruption history

title: Morph ingest: gzip decompression fails on files with trailing padding bytes

Found during the full-library run: 203 failures in one window, confirmed via a real file (DAZ 3D/Genesis 3/Female/Morphs/3DArena/3DA Nails Square.dsf, 19 trailing space bytes) that decompresses fine via low-level zlib.decompressobj (eof=True, trailing bytes in unused_data) but failed via gzip.open.
acceptance_criteria: parse_dsf_file successfully parses gzip .dsf files with trailing garbage after the stream. FIXED: switched to zlib.decompressobj(16+MAX_WBITS), test added with synthetic trailing-padding fixture, verified against the real failing file.
close_reason: Switched _read_dsf_text to zlib.decompressobj, discards trailing garbage via unused_data instead of treating it as a second gzip member

title: Morph ingest: .tmb format can't represent DAZ's vertex_count=-1 sentinel

Discovered during the same full-library smoke run that found the gzip bug (daz-content-browser-d3y).

Update the design doc's .tmb binary spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-morph-ingest-transpiler-design.md section 5) to note vertex_count is signed and -1 is a valid DSON sentinel meaning 'unspecified/same as base'.
acceptance_criteria: write_tmb/read_tmb round-trip vertex_count=-1 correctly (change the header's vertex_count field from unsigned to signed 32-bit). Test coverage for the negative-vertex_count case using a real-shaped example.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8a66eac (signed int32 vertex_count in .tmb header), verified against real library

title: Morph ingest: support gzip-compressed .dsf files
description: parse_dsf_file (src/dsf_parser.py) assumes plain UTF-8 JSON text, but DAZ .dsf files may be gzip-compressed (the format explicitly supports this, and the original spec said 'Reads uncompressed/gzipped .dsf files'). Discovered during a full-library smoke run against the user's real ~321K-file library: a random sample of 500 real .dsf files showed 184/500 (37%) are gzip-compressed, all currently failing to parse with UnicodeDecodeError and being silently skipped as per-file errors. This is a systematic data-loss bug, not an edge case -- undetected earlier because both test fixtures happen to be plain-text.
design: Peek the first 2 bytes of the file; if they match the gzip magic number (0x1f 0x8b), decompress via the gzip module before JSON parsing; otherwise read as plain UTF-8 text as today.
acceptance_criteria: parse_dsf_file transparently handles both plain-text and gzip-compressed .dsf files (detected via gzip magic bytes, not file extension/naming). Test coverage for both cases using real or synthetic gzip-compressed fixtures.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 7f2ea50 (zlib-based gzip detection in _read_dsf_text), verified against real library

title: Fix DirectML GPU acceleration silently falling back to CPU
description: Provider logging (daz-content-browser-67l) revealed DmlExecutionProvider was unreachable: chromadb and optimum both pull in plain onnxruntime transitively, which shares its import namespace with onnxruntime-directml, and whichever gets installed last silently wins. install.py's docs also still claimed CPU-only, left over from before the DIM-packaging commit (de19ddc) switched pyproject.toml's intent to DirectML-with-CPU-fallback. Force-reinstall onnxruntime-directml last in install.py/Makefile so it reliably wins, and update docs/messages to reflect GPU-with-fallback. Benchmarked ~7.3x faster embedding inference on DirectML vs CPU once warmed up (0.59ms/item vs 4.32ms/item).
design: Root cause: onnxruntime and onnxruntime-directml are separate PyPI packages sharing the 'onnxruntime' import path; pip has no way to express their mutual exclusivity, so transitive deps (chromadb, optimum) silently reinstall plain onnxruntime over the intended DirectML build with no error or warning at install time.

title: Subsystem C: Scene Lifecycle & Persistence
description:
Implements the JIT morph loader's Subsystem C per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-jit-morph-loader-parent-spec.md section 4.3: persists which morphs InjectorCore has injected into the scene (guid + current value) so that closing and reopening a .duf file restores them without native Daz Studio missing-file dialogs (since the morphs' .dsf source files are never actually loaded/referenced by the saved scene -- only their .tmb-derived deltas were injected in-memory by Subsystem B). Depends on Subsystem B (beads-2mw, done) for InjectorCore::injectMorphByGuid and the daz_plugin CMake target.

CORRECTIONS AGAINST REAL SDK HEADERS (found before filing these tasks, since Subsystem B's own design pass found the parent spec's original sketches didn't always match the real SDK -- checked the same way here rather than assuming):
- The parent spec's sketch names a signal 'aboutToLoadScene()' -- this does NOT exist in dzscene.h. The real signals are 'sceneLoadStarting()' and 'sceneLoaded()' (dzscene.h, confirmed against daz-studio-45-sdk-win32). There's also 'sceneSaveStarting()'/'sceneSaved()' for the save side, which the parent spec's sketch didn't mention at all but which this subsystem needs (to snapshot the manifest before it's written).
- The parent spec's sketch calls 'dzScene->setUpdateAllManagers(false)' to suspend viewport/property recalculation during batch reinjection -- this method does NOT exist anywhere in the SDK (grepped the full include/ tree). No scene-wide update-suspension mechanism was found. Whatever performance strategy this subsystem uses must be re-derived against real APIs, not assumed from the parent spec.
- DzCustomData (dzcustomdata.h) is real, but it's a subclassable base class with virtual loadSection()/save() for custom binary serialization -- not a simple 'attach a JSON string' API as the parent spec's payload sketch implies. The actual attach/retrieve mechanism is DzElement::addDataItem(DzElementData*)/findDataItem(QString) (dzelement.h), which DzScene inherits (confirmed live in a running Daz Studio instance during Subsystem B's testing, on a DzModifier instance -- the same mechanism applies to any DzElement including DzScene).
- The parent spec's injection sequence mentions 'parallel threads where safe' for batch injection -- this contradicts Subsystem B's own established, binding threading rule (design doc section 7: all Daz Studio SDK scene-graph mutations occur on the main GUI thread only; only TmbReader's mmap file read may happen off-thread). Subsystem C's batch-reinjection-on-load must respect this same constraint -- no naive multithreading of SDK object construction.

title: Skip re-embedding unchanged products on full reindex
description:
Full reindex (--all/--force) re-embeds every product's embedding_text on each run, even when most products are unchanged since the last index. This wastes ONNX inference time and ChromaDB upsert work at scale.

Add a checksum (e.g. sha256) of embedding_text per SKU, stored alongside the product row in SQLite. During generate_and_store_embeddings(), compare the new checksum against the stored one and skip embedding+upsert for SKUs whose text hasn't changed. Only embed new/changed/missing-from-Chroma SKUs.

This is a cheaper, more broadly impactful win than the existing I/O pipelining optimization (daz-content-browser-8wq) since it avoids the embedding work entirely for unchanged items rather than just overlapping it.
close_reason: Incorrect premise: incremental update only ever processes brand-new SKUs (postgres_skus - sqlite_skus), never re-touches existing ones, so there's nothing unchanged to skip there. --force/--all is intentionally a from-scratch rebuild, so checksum-skipping would undermine its purpose. No real benefit.

title: Add Daz Studio 6 SDK build support to daz_plugin's CMake (lib-path convention + Qt6 acquisition)
description:
Follow-up from beads-2mw.10, which found daz_plugin's C++ code is almost entirely SDK6-compatible (verified by diffing dzformula.h/dzerclink.h/dznumericcontroller.h/dznumericproperty.h/dzmorph.h/dzmorphdeltas.h/dzobject.h/dzplugin.h between daz-studio-45-sdk-win32 and daz-studio-6-sdk-win32) but the BUILD LAYER (cpp/cmake/DazStudioSDK.cmake) is not, because it was written assuming SDK 4.5's directory/Qt-vendoring conventions:

1. Lib path convention differs: SDK 4.5 uses lib/<plat>/dzcore.lib, SDK6 uses <plat>/lib/dzcore.lib. DazStudioSDK.cmake hardcodes the former.
2. Qt acquisition differs entirely: SDK 4.5 vendors Qt 4.8 directly inside the SDK (no external Qt needed). SDK6 ships no Qt of its own at all -- requires a separately-installed Qt6 devkit via find_package(Qt6) and a user-supplied Qt6_DIR cache var (see the sibling daz-script-server project's build.sh/.env for an already-working pattern: aqtinstall to get a matching Qt6 minor version, then --sdk-version 6 selects a separate build-sdk6/ directory).
3. DZSDK_QT_SCRIPT_TARGET maps to Qt4::QtScript on SDK 4.5 but Qt6::Qml on SDK6 (QtScript was removed from Qt entirely) -- daz_plugin currently links QtScript per the AFirstPlugin sample pattern; check at implementation time whether it's actually used at runtime or can be dropped for the SDK6 build.

Confirmed compatible and requiring NO source changes: DzFormula/DzFormulaController (Operation enum, Stage enum, addFormula), DzERCLink (ERCType/ERCKeyInterpolation values unchanged, just explicitly typed now), DzMorphDeltas::addDeltas (both overloads we use, including checkForDuplicates default, unchanged), DzObject::findModifier/addModifier/removeModifier.

One thing worth doing proactively regardless of full SDK6 support: DzMorph::getValueChannel() (used in InjectorCore.cpp) is marked '// TODO : SDK 6 : remove' in the SDK6 header, with a new getValueControl() method as its apparent replacement, immediately above it. Still present and working today, but on a documented deprecation path.
acceptance_criteria: daz_plugin builds cleanly against DAZ_SDK_DIR pointed at daz-studio-6-sdk-win32 with a real, externally-supplied Qt6 devkit, using the same source files as the SDK 4.5 build (no #ifdef needed for the classes/methods audited in beads-2mw.10, per that issue's findings) -- only cpp/cmake/DazStudioSDK.cmake (or a parallel variant selected by SDK version) needs new logic for the lib path convention and Qt6 acquisition.

title: PropertySourceAdapter drops the DSON label prefix, risking wrong-node resolution across companion figures with duplicate bone names
description:
Found via live exploration while investigating the spline-formula path (never yet runtime-verified). PropertySourceAdapter::parseOperand deliberately drops the label prefix before the colon in an operand URL (e.g. the 'Genesis9' in 'Genesis9/l_eye:/data/.../Genesis9.dsf#l_eye?rotation/y') -- per its own design comment, matching Subsystem A's extract_referenced_guids() which also drops it. Node resolution then falls through to a scene-wide dzScene->findNode(elementName) search when no closer match is found.

Genesis 9 content routinely loads several companion figures parented/synced to the main figure (Genesis9Eyelashes, Genesis9Tear, Genesis9Eyes, Genesis9Mouth, G9EyebrowFibers), each of which duplicates the base figure's bone names for rigging/skinning purposes. Confirmed live in the current test scene: 7 distinct DzBone nodes all named 'l_eye' exist simultaneously (one per figure). A bare Scene.findNode('l_eye') happened to resolve to the correct one (Genesis9's own) in this scene, but that appears to depend on Daz's internal node-registration/search order rather than any documented, guaranteed-stable contract -- if a companion figure's bone were registered/indexed such that it shadowed the base figure's, a cross-figure formula operand like the FICairo_head_cbs_EyesLSideOut example (driven by 'Genesis9/l_eye', but attached to a morph on the Genesis9Eyes figure) could silently resolve to the WRONG l_eye bone (e.g. Genesis9Eyes' own, rather than Genesis9's), producing a live-reactive but semantically wrong result -- not a crash, a silent misattachment in the same family as beads-w56/beads-2kv.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) confirm empirically across multiple real scenes/load orders that dzScene->findNode() has a stable, documented-enough resolution priority (e.g. always prefers the top-level/primary figure) that makes dropping the label safe in practice, and record that finding so this can be closed with confidence, or (b) stop dropping the label prefix -- use it to scope the node search to the correct figure's own hierarchy (e.g. resolve the label against Scene's node list first, then search within that figure specifically) before falling back to the current scene-wide search.
notes: Lower priority than beads-w56/beads-2kv: this is a theoretical risk confirmed structurally possible (7 same-named bones exist) but NOT yet observed to actually misfire -- the one live test we ran resolved correctly. Not blocking; worth a follow-up pass once the spline-formula path itself gets its first runtime verification (which will exercise exactly this cross-figure resolution case).

title: Subsystem B Task 10 (non-blocking): Confirm Studio 6 SDK header parity
description: Once daz_plugin builds cleanly against daz-studio-45-sdk-win32 (Task 5), attempt building the same cpp/daz_plugin target against DAZ_SDK_DIR pointed at daz-studio-6-sdk-win32 (and ideally the macos variants of both, if a macOS toolchain is available) to confirm dzformula.h/dzerclink.h/dznumericcontroller.h/dznumericproperty.h/dzmorph.h/dzmorphdeltas.h expose the same classes/signatures relied on throughout Subsystem B. Design doc §4/§5 note this is expected but unconfirmed. Not on the critical path -- only blocks claiming cross-version SDK compatibility, not Subsystem B's core functionality.
design: Design doc §5 CMake/Build Layout note on multi-SDK-variant support.
acceptance_criteria: Either: builds cleanly against Studio 6 win32 with no source changes (parity confirmed, update the design doc's §5 note), or: specific header differences are documented (which classes/signatures differ) so a follow-up issue can be filed for #ifdef handling.
notes:
RESULT: parity NOT confirmed -- real, structural differences found. Actually attempted the build (cmake -S cpp -B cpp/build-sdk6 -DDAZ_SDK_DIR=<daz-studio-6-sdk-win32>) and it fails at configure time, plus diffed the exact headers/signatures Subsystem B depends on between the two SDKs.

=== 1. BUILD LAYOUT -- fails immediately, no source changes possible without new CMake work ===
cpp/cmake/DazStudioSDK.cmake (written for SDK 4.5) hardcodes DAZ_SDK_CORE_RELATIVE_PATH = "lib/${DZ_MIXED_PLATFORM}/dzcore.lib" (i.e. lib/x64/dzcore.lib). SDK6's own top-level CMakeLists.txt uses the OPPOSITE order: "${DZ_MIXED_PLATFORM}/lib/dzcore.lib" (i.e. x64/lib/dzcore.lib) -- confirmed by both the actual directory layout (x64/lib/, x64/bin/, vs SDK 4.5's lib/x64/, bin/x64/) and by reading SDK6's CMakeLists.txt directly. Configure fails immediately: "The library dzcore could not be located at .../lib/x64/dzcore.lib".

=== 2. QT ACQUISITION -- fundamentally different model, not just a path change ===
SDK 4.5 vendors Qt 4.8 directly inside the SDK (lib/<plat>/Qt*4.lib, bin/<plat>/Qt*4.dll) -- our DazStudioSDK.cmake declares Qt4::* imported targets straight from those files, no external Qt install needed. SDK6 ships NO Qt libs of its own at all (only dzcore.lib + dzsdkmemory.lib) -- confirmed empty x64/lib/ apart from those two files. SDK6's own CMakeLists.txt requires a SEPARATE, externally-installed Qt6 devkit via find_package(Qt6 ...) and a user-supplied Qt6_DIR cache var pointing at a real Qt6Config.cmake (matches what the sibling daz-script-server project's own docs already say: 'pip install aqtinstall; aqt install-qt windows desktop 6.10.3 win64_msvc2022_64 -m qt5compat'). This is a different acquisition model entirely, not a path tweak.

=== 3. QT MODULE TARGET RENAMES -- QtScript is GONE, replaced by QML ===
SDK 4.5's DZSDK_QT_SCRIPT_TARGET = Qt4::QtScript. SDK6's equivalent DZSDK_QT_SCRIPT_TARGET = Qt6::Qml -- Qt dropped QtScript entirely between Qt4 and Qt6; Daz's SDK6 CMakeLists.txt maps the same variable name onto the QML module instead. Also DZSDK_QT_CORE_TARGET becomes a TWO-target list (Qt6::Core Qt6::Core5Compat, for Qt5-compat shims) instead of SDK 4.5's single Qt4::QtCore. A new DZSDK_QT_UI_TOOLS_TARGET (Qt6::UiTools) exists with no SDK 4.5 equivalent.

=== 4. HEADER/SIGNATURE DIFFERENCES IN THE SPECIFIC CLASSES SUBSYSTEM B USES ===
Diffed dzformula.h, dzerclink.h, dznumericcontroller.h, dznumericproperty.h, dzmorph.h, dzmorphdeltas.h, dzobject.h, dzplugin.h directly between both SDKs:

- DzFormula::Operation enum, DzFormulaController::Stage enum + addFormula() signature: IDENTICAL (whitespace-only diff).
- DzERCLink: ERCType/ERCKeyInterpolation enum VALUES unchanged, but now explicitly typed  in SDK6 (was implicit int) -- harmless for us, we only compare/pass the enum. setScalar/setAddend/setType/setKeyInterpolation/addKeyValue signatures unchanged; setProperty and addKeyValue gained Q_SLOT/Q_INVOKABLE annotations (Qt reflection metadata for DazScript access) -- no C++ call-site impact.
- DzNumericController::apply(): signature unchanged, gained Q_INVOKABLE.
- DzNumericProperty::insertController(): SIGNATURE CHANGED -- SDK 4.5 returns void, SDK6 returns bool (and gained Q_SLOT). Our FormulaControllerBuilder.cpp calls this without using a return value, so this does NOT break compilation, but SDK6 added a way to detect insertController failure that our current code silently ignores -- worth adopting when SDK6 support is actually built, not just noted.
- DzMorph::getValueChannel(): present in SDK6 but the header comment reads "// TODO : SDK 6 : remove" -- Daz's own SDK authors have flagged this exact method (which InjectorCore::injectRecord depends on) for future removal. A new getValueControl() method appears immediately above it in the SDK6 header, clearly its intended replacement. This is the single most important forward-compatibility risk found: works today on SDK6, but is on a deprecation path.
- DzMorphDeltas::addDeltas(): the two overloads we could use are unchanged (checkForDuplicates defaulted true in BOTH SDKs, contrary to what might be assumed); SDK6 purely ADDS a third convenience overload (addDeltas(const DzMorphDelta*, int)) we don't use.
- DzObject::findModifier/addModifier/removeModifier: signatures unchanged (parameter name/const-ref formatting only).
- DzPlugin macros: DZ_PLUGIN_DEFINITION, DZ_PLUGIN_AUTHOR, DZ_PLUGIN_VERSION, DZ_PLUGIN_DESCRIPTION, DZ_PLUGIN_CLASS_GUID (all five actually used in PluginMain.cpp) are present in SDK6 with the same names. SDK6 removes DZ_PLUGIN_CLASS_GUID_OWNED/DZ_PLUGIN_CUSTOM_CLASS_GUID_OWNED (not used by us) and adds several new macros (gadget/enum/flag/sequence factories, ref-counted variants) not used by us either.

=== CONCLUSION ===
The SDK class APIs Subsystem B actually calls are almost entirely compatible (one non-breaking return-type widening on insertController, one flagged-for-future-removal method still present and working). The real blocker to cross-SDK-version support is entirely at the BUILD/CMAKE layer -- the lib path convention and the Qt acquisition model are both incompatible with the current single DazStudioSDK.cmake module, which was written assuming SDK 4.5's vendored-Qt-inside-SDK layout. Supporting SDK6 would need: (a) a path-convention branch in DazStudioSDK.cmake (or a parallel DazStudioSDK6.cmake) keyed on some detectable SDK-version signal, (b) a find_package(Qt6) path requiring the user to separately provide Qt6_DIR (matching the sibling daz-script-server project's already-proven pattern for this), and (c) remapping DZSDK_QT_SCRIPT_TARGET from QtScript to Qml if daz_plugin ever actually uses that module (currently it links QtCore/QtGui/QtScript per the AFirstPlugin sample pattern -- worth checking at that time whether QtScript's actual runtime usage, if any, has a real Qt6/QML equivalent needed, or whether it can just be dropped from the link line for SDK6). No code changes to injector_core or daz_plugin's actual C++ logic are needed for the classes verified here; migrate getValueChannel() -> getValueControl() proactively when SDK6 support is built, since the old one is on a documented deprecation path.
close_reason: Actually attempted the SDK6 build (not just theorized) and diffed all the specific headers Subsystem B depends on. Parity is NOT full -- build layer (lib path convention, Qt acquisition model) is incompatible and needs new CMake work, tracked separately as beads-31u. Class-level API differences are minor/non-breaking (one insertController return-type widening, one deprecated-but-present method). Full findings in notes; design doc updated.

title: Morph ingest: add retry/error visibility for embed_and_store_morphs failures
description: embed_and_store_morphs (src/managers/morph_transpiler.py) returns only an embedded count; unlike its sibling generate_and_store_embeddings (src/managers/postgres_db_manager.py) which returns a success/failure bool, a fully-failed embed batch is invisible to the CLI (src/main.py discards the return value). Combined with incremental mode only ever passing new_guids to the embed step, a batch that fails after SQLite has already committed those rows is never retried on a later run (hashes match, so it's skipped) -- a permanent gap with no equivalent of 'vab load --phase embed' to repair it for morphs.
acceptance_criteria: Caller can detect a partial/failed embed run (e.g. non-zero exit code or explicit log/warning), and there's a documented way to re-embed already-ingested-but-not-embedded morphs (a --phase-embed-only style flag, or a query for SQLite-guids-missing-from-Chroma using the existing ChromaDbManager.get_all_ids()).
close_reason: Fixed: embed_and_store_morphs returns failed_guids, CLI surfaces embed failures in summary

title: Morph ingest: harden incremental cache against stale/moved/deleted files
description: Several related incremental-mode gaps found during final review of the morph ingest pipeline (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-06-morph-ingest-transpiler.md): (1) the skip-on-hash-match branch never checks that the referenced .tmb file still exists on disk, so deleting morph_cache/ alone (without also touching morph_index.db) leaves rows pointing at missing files that a future consumer would fail to read; (2) a .dsf moved within the library (same mtime+size, different path) is skipped as unchanged, leaving a stale source_dsf_path/tmb_path; (3) .dsf files deleted from the library are never pruned from morphs/morph_cache -- only --force clears everything. (4) morph_cache/ is not in .gitignore, so a default-path run drops a large untracked tree in the repo root -- fix this one immediately, it's a one-line addition.
acceptance_criteria: morph_cache/ added to .gitignore. At least the missing-.tmb-file case (1) is detected and triggers re-ingest of that row rather than silently trusting a stale hash match.
close_reason: Fixed: skip-on-hash-match now checks .tmb file exists, re-ingests if missing

title: Morph ingest: validate --library-path before destructive --force actions
description: In morphs_index_command (src/main.py) and index_library (src/managers/morph_transpiler.py), a typo'd --library-path with --force currently: resets the Chroma collection, deletes morph_cache/, creates/wipes morph_index.db, and only THEN raises FileNotFoundError when data/ isn't found under the given path. The destructive actions should happen after path validation, not before.
acceptance_criteria: A --force run with a nonexistent --library-path fails fast with no destructive side effects (Chroma collection intact, morph_cache/ and morph_index.db untouched).
close_reason: Extracted validate_library_root(), called before any destructive --force action in both index_library and the CLI, verified with test + manual CLI check

title: Morph ingest: scope name-marker dependency resolution to target_figure, not global name
description: rebuild_dependencies' name_to_id lookup (src/managers/morph_index_manager.py) is keyed globally on morph name, but DAZ morph names (e.g. pJCM* joint-corrective morphs) repeat across different base figures (Genesis 8 vs Genesis 9). A pathless formula ref (name:X) can therefore bind to a same-named morph on the wrong figure. Should be keyed on (target_figure, name) instead. Found during final-review fix-wave re-review; rated Minor only because morph_dependencies has no consumer yet, but becomes real the moment anything reads the graph (e.g. the future C++ injector).
acceptance_criteria: rebuild_dependencies resolves name: markers scoped to the dependent morph's own target_figure, with a test proving two same-named morphs on different figures don't cross-resolve.
close_reason: Scoped name_to_id lookup to (target_figure, name) in rebuild_dependencies, test added and passing

title: CLI Progress/Rich spinner crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on cp1252 Windows terminals
description: Both 'vab load' and the new 'vab morphs index' use rich.progress.Progress with a SpinnerColumn. On a Windows terminal running the legacy cp1252 codepage (not UTF-8 console mode), Rich's spinner cleanup on Progress.__exit__ raises UnicodeEncodeError ('charmap' codec can't encode character u2826) when writing the braille spinner glyph. Discovered while smoke-testing the new morphs index command against a real DAZ library subset (X:\DAZ Libraries\Project data) — the underlying ingest/embed work completed successfully (verified 70/70 morphs in SQLite + Chroma) but the process then crashed with a traceback instead of printing the final summary line. Pre-existing in load_command's identical Progress setup; not introduced by the morph ingest work, just newly triggered by it.
acceptance_criteria: vab load and vab morphs index both complete cleanly (exit 0, summary printed) on a Windows terminal running the default cp1252 codepage, e.g. by disabling Rich's legacy Windows rendering or forcing UTF-8 output mode.
close_reason: Fixed: force UTF-8 stdout/stderr before rendering Progress bars, eliminates cp1252 UnicodeEncodeError crash

title: Scope standalone CLI/offline indexer (no DAZ Studio, no FastAPI server)
description: Discussed with user: a standalone tool for users with very large content libraries to pre-build the index outside of DAZ Studio, avoiding resource contention with DAZ's own CPU/GPU usage while indexing runs. Key insight from discussion: the indexing logic is already factored into a reusable function (run_update_flow in api_tasks.py), so this is cheap to build as a thin CLI entry point calling it directly -- no FastAPI server needed. The GPU/threading speed itself benefits equally whether called from the server or a standalone tool (DirectML/threading work helps both paths identically) -- the standalone tool's real value is avoiding contention with DAZ Studio's own resource usage, not raw speed. Would need packaging as an optional DIM (similar to the existing export-tool package pattern in release.py) and the settings dialog should clearly show when an index was built externally so users aren't confused about why 'Update Index' shows nothing new to do. Not yet scoped in detail -- needs a design pass before implementation.

title: Pipeline embed-loop I/O with compute (overlap SQLite reads/Chroma writes with ONNX inference)
description: Discussed as a follow-up to the DirectML fix (daz-content-browser-0ce/i8z): generate_and_store_embeddings (postgres_db_manager.py:217-292) does SQLite read -> ONNX embed -> ChromaDB upsert sequentially per batch with no overlap. Now that DirectML is confirmed genuinely active and fast (~7.3x vs CPU), the SQLite/Chroma I/O around it is proportionally larger and may be worth overlapping with a producer/consumer pattern (prefetch next batch's SQLite read while current batch embeds/writes). Keep ChromaDB upserts serialized since its local SQLite-backed store isn't documented-safe for concurrent writers. Lower priority now than before the DML fix landed, since GPU embedding speed reduced how much this matters in absolute terms — re-evaluate with a real end-to-end timing breakdown (load/etl/embed stage durations) before committing to the added complexity.
notes: Added per-stage timing breakdown (sqlite_read/embed/chroma_upsert) to generate_and_store_embeddings, logged at end of each run. Issue stays OPEN until a real indexing run's breakdown is captured and reviewed to decide if overlap is worth the complexity.
close_reason: Measured with real instrumentation added for this issue (per-stage timing in generate_and_store_embeddings). Two full 4269-product reindex runs post-DirectML-fix: ETL ~2m38-39s, embed-loop ~26-27.5s total with sqlite_read=0.0s (0%), embed=23-24.5s (89%), chroma_upsert=2.9-3.0s (11%). SQLite read time is negligible/unmeasurable, so there is no meaningful I/O to overlap with compute — embed-loop is compute-bound on ONNX/DirectML inference, not I/O-bound. Producer/consumer prefetch would add complexity for no measurable gain. Not pursuing.

title: Verify DirectML actually executes inference (not just selected) via ORT profiling
description: After fixing the onnxruntime-directml install-order bug (daz-content-browser-0ce), Windows GPU performance counters showed zero usage for vab.exe during a live indexing run, raising doubt about whether DmlExecutionProvider was genuinely executing compute or just reported as 'active' by session.get_providers() (which only reflects configured/available providers, not actual per-node execution). Added an opt-in diagnostic (EMBEDDING_PROFILE_PROVIDERS=1) using ONNX Runtime's own execution profiler to log per-provider node count and duration. Verified inside the actual frozen vab.exe (not just the dev venv): DmlExecutionProvider executes 1616 of 2212 graph nodes, CPUExecutionProvider only the remaining 596 (normal unsupported ops like reshapes). Same split confirmed in both the venv and the bundled executable. Conclusion: DirectML is genuinely active; the earlier zero-GPU-counter reading was a Windows performance-counter sampling artifact (misses brief/bursty workloads), not a real CPU fallback.
acceptance_criteria: EMBEDDING_PROFILE_PROVIDERS=1 diagnostic added to embedding_utils.py, off by default; verified via test_embedding.py and tests/test_api.py passing; provider split confirmed identical in dev venv and frozen vab.exe.
close_reason: Confirmed via ORT execution profiler inside the actual frozen vab.exe: DmlExecutionProvider runs 1616/2212 graph nodes, identical split to the dev venv. GPU question settled - DirectML is genuinely active.

title: Quantize ONNX model to reduce DIM package size
description: The current model.onnx (bge-large-en-v1.5) is 1.3GB in float32. Applying ONNX dynamic quantization to int8 would reduce it to approximately 300-400MB, bringing the total DIM zip from ~900MB to around 400-500MB. Use onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic with QuantType.QInt8. Should be added as a step in export_model.py with a --quantize flag, and evaluated for search quality impact.
